deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let K = π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) = ⟨l0,l1,l∞ | l0 l1 l∞ = 1⟩, discrete or profinite. Grothendieck works inside the extension of S3 by K, the 'automorphic' fundamental group of the orbifold (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S3. Concretely this is the subgroup of Aut(K) generated by Int(K) and lifts σ0, σ1, σ∞ of the transpositions of {0,1,∞}, together with a lift ρ of the 3-cycle. Each σ_i fixes the loop l_i. As announced on p.12, an element g ∈ K is identified with int(g).

The ε_i. On p.12 he looks for square roots of the loops of the form ε_i = (inner)·σ_i·(inner). He finds that the twisting exponent α ∈ Ẑ must be 1, giving
- ε∞ = l0 σ∞ l∞
- ε0 = l1 σ0 l0
- ε1 = l∞ σ1 l1

This page.
1. He records ε_i^2 = l_i for i = 0, 1, ∞.
2. Solving for σ_i, and using σ_i = σ_i^{-1}, gives σ0 = ε0 ε1^2, σ1 = ε1 ε∞^2, σ∞ = ε∞ ε0^2. Check: from ε∞ = l0 σ∞ l∞ one gets σ∞ = ε0^{-2} ε∞^{-1}, whose inverse is ε∞ ε0^2.
3. Translating l0 l1 l∞ = 1 and σ_i^2 = 1 gives the relations ε0^2 ε1^2 ε∞^2 = 1 and (ε0 ε1^2)^2 = (ε1 ε∞^2)^2 = (ε∞ ε0^2)^2 = 1.
4. The 3-cycle is defined by σ0σ1 = l1^{-1} ρ. Hence ρ = l1 σ0 σ1 = ε1^2 ε0 ε1^2 · ε1 ε∞^2. Since ε1^2 ε∞^2 = ε0^{-2}, this is ρ = ε1^2 ε0 ε1 ε0^{-2}. By cyclic symmetry ρ = ε∞^2 ε1 ε∞ ε1^{-2} = ε0^2 ε∞ ε0 ε∞^{-2}.
5. He notes in the margin that these three expressions do not seem to follow from the previous relations.
6. He multiplies the three expressions in reverse order. The inner factors ε∞^{-2}ε∞^2 and ε1^{-2}ε1^2 cancel, giving ρ^3 = ε0^2 (ε∞ ε0 ε1)^2 ε0^{-2}. So ρ^3 = 1 forces (ε0 ε1 ε∞)^2 = 1.
7. He finds this 'inquiétant': the sentence continues on p.14, apparently 'no element of finite order' in these groups. That would force ε0 ε1 ε∞ = 1, which p.14 first boxes, then crosses out, then replaces by the guess ε0 ε1 ε∞ = σ1, also crossed out. He then turns to a critique distinguishing discrete from profinite groups.

Modern interpretation. In the discrete case the extension is PSL2(Z) ⊃ Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F2, with quotient S3. Explicitly take:
- l∞ = T^2, ε∞ = T = [[1,1],[0,1]]
- ε0 = [[1,0],[-1,1]], with ε0^2 = l0 = [[1,0],[-2,1]]
- ε1 = [[0,1],[-1,2]], the parabolic square root of l1 = (l∞ l0)^{-1}, fixing the cusp 1.

Then ε0 ε1 ε∞ = [[0,1],[-1,0]] = S, an involution. Equivalently, under B3 → SL2(Z) the ε's are the three half-twists σ2, σ2^{-1}σ1σ2, σ1. Their product is the Garside element Δ = σ1σ2σ1, and Δ^2 is central, hence trivial in PSL2(Z). So (ε0ε1ε∞)^2 = 1 is correct and not alarming: the group does have torsion beyond conjugates of the σ_i, namely S and ρ. The guess 'ε0ε1ε∞ = σ1' points in the right direction, since the product is an involution. The rejected 'ε0ε1ε∞ = 1' is false under this normalisation.

Purpose. The computation is part of setting up the S3-equivariant structure on π̂1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with a Ẑ-parameter α. This is the structure through which Gal(Q̄/Q) acts. It is the same kind of bookkeeping later encoded in the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of Drinfeld–Ihara's Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (λ ∈ Ẑ*, m = (λ−1)/2).
errors: The page's own algebra checks out: the inversions of the σ_i, the ρ expressions and the derivation of (ε0ε1ε∞)^2 = 1 are all correct.
The three cyclic expressions for ρ assume σ1σ∞ = l∞^{-1}ρ and σ∞σ0 = l0^{-1}ρ, by symmetry with σ0σ1 = l1^{-1}ρ; these are not verified on the page.

The worry 'il n'y a pas d'élément [d'ordre fini]' is mistaken: the extension of S3 by K (discrete model PSL2(Z)) contains torsion other than conjugates of the σ_i. With the natural normalisation, ε0ε1ε∞ is the involution S (the image of the Garside element Δ of B3), not 1.
The subsequent boxed 'ε0ε1ε∞ = 1' on p.14 would be an error; Grothendieck himself crosses it out.

ideas.what: Square roots ε_i of the cusp loops l_i in the S3-extension of π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}), each a lift of the transposition σ_i twisted by inner automorphisms, with ε_i^2 = l_i.
ideas.modern_name: Parabolic generators of PSL2(Z) (T and its conjugates) / half-twists in B3 mod centre; Γ(2) ⊂ PSL2(Z) with quotient S3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); the braid-group description is Artin-era
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Γ_{0,4}, Γ_{1,1} = SL2(Z) and the S3-action, but not this explicit computation

ideas.what: Presentation of the extension in terms of the ε_i: ε0^2ε1^2ε∞^2 = 1, (ε_iε_j^2)^2 = 1, ρ^3 = 1, leading to (ε0ε1ε∞)^2 = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of PSL2(Z) ≅ B3/Z(B3) via three half-twists, where Δ^2 is central

ideas.what: S3-equivariant normalisation of lifts with a parameter α ∈ Ẑ (fixed to α = 1 on p.12), as preparation for the Galois action on π̂1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).
ideas.modern_name: Precursor of the 2-cycle/3-cycle (hexagon) relations defining the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and the Galois action, without these formulas

missed.claim: This is a dated 1981 manuscript instance of Grothendieck computing the S3-equivariant structure of π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with an α ∈ Ẑ parameter and half-twist square roots of the cusp loops. That bookkeeping later underlies the hexagon relations of GT. The mathematics itself is classical (PSL2(Z), B3), and the page ends in a confusion that he then critiques.
missed.quote: multipliant ces relations dans l'ordre inverse et écrivant ρ^3 = 1, on trouve (ε0ε1ε∞)^2 = 1 ce qui est inquiétant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents pre-Esquisse explicit work toward a GT-type description of the S3-symmetry of the Galois action on the tripod's fundamental group. It does not contain a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are elementary group theory recovering the classical PSL2(Z)/B3 structure of the S3-extension of the free group. The only interest is historical: early (1981) explicit groundwork resembling GT relations. The page's own worry stems from an incorrect expectation of torsion-freeness.
transcription_corrections: The final sentence continues on p.14 as 'il n'y a pas d'élément d'[ordre?] fini dans les groupes …'. Mathematically 'ordre fini' (finite order) fits better than 'indice fini'; the reading is uncertain.
Line 'On obtient ρ [-...-] par': a word is struck out after ρ, apparently ending in 'p…'; illegible.
Second line of the ρ computation reads ρ = ε1^2 ε0 ε1^2 ε1 ε∞^2, regrouped as ε1^2 ε0 ε1 (ε1^2 ε∞^2) with the brace labelled ε0^{-2}. The transcription is consistent with this.
Struck-out line: 'ρ = σ0σ1 = σ1σ∞ = σ∞σ0', with '=' written below and then 'ε0ε1^3ε∞' (last factor partly illegible), all struck.
